clue.text: Works out Princess Royal is Olympic athlete

parts.note: to figure out a sum is to work it out, so works out gives figures
Kate, the Princess of Wales

explanation.surface: A list of credentials: the Princess Royal does her workouts and turns out to be an Olympian.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Princess Royal' reads as Princess Anne's title, but it splits: Kate is a princess and R stands for royal.
explanation.definitionFit: Figure skating is an Olympic winter sport, so its competitor is one kind of Olympic athlete.

clue.text: Female ne'er-do-well upset woodcutter

indicators.note: in a down clue, upset means turned upside down, so the word is read from the bottom up

parts.note: a waster is a lazy good-for-nothing

explanation.surface: A woman with a layabout partner is upset about a lumberjack.
explanation.definitionFit: A fretsaw is a fine-bladed saw used for cutting curved shapes in thin wood.

clue.text: Left organised grand uprising — one is seen in Knotty Ash?

definitions.text: one is seen in Knotty Ash?

indicators.note: in a down clue an uprising means the letters climb, reading bottom to top

parts.note: to run a business is to organise it, so organised gives ran
G is slang shorthand for a grand, a thousand pounds

explanation.surface: Political unrest in Knotty Ash, the Liverpool suburb made famous by comedian Ken Dodd.
explanation.walkthrough: Knotty Ash is a real Liverpool district, but here it is read as knotted ash wood.
explanation.definitionFit: A gnarl is a knotty protuberance on a tree, so ash timber full of knots would show one.

clue.text: I earn a lot jiggling, in theory

indicators.note: jiggling shakes the letters of these words about into a fresh order

explanation.surface: A boast that one earns a fortune by jiggling, at least on paper.
explanation.definitionFit: A rationale is the underlying reasoning or principle behind something, a theory of why it is done.

clue.text: Small animal dropping

parts.note: a cat is an animal

explanation.surface: A little creature falling, or perhaps being dropped.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Dropping' looks like a verb, but it is a noun: what an animal leaves behind.
explanation.definitionFit: Scat is the term trackers use for animal dung, a dropping.

clue.text: Outrageous report of two canines getting drink before meal

indicators.note: the sound match is a stretch, an outrageous one, so the clue owns up to a loose spoken version

parts.note: canines are pointed teeth, so two of them are a pair of teeth, said loosely as a pair o' teeth

explanation.surface: A shocking news story about two dogs having a drink before dinner.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Canines' suggests dogs, but here they are teeth; 'a pair o' teeth' said quickly is the answer, which the setter admits is outrageous.
explanation.definitionFit: An aperitif is an alcoholic drink taken to stimulate the appetite before eating.

clue.text: Stop old women getting grant

parts.note: to end something is to stop it

explanation.surface: Cutting off funding for elderly women's grants.
explanation.definitionFit: To endow is to give a fund or income to an institution, a grant of money.

clue.text: Hopeful spat with Iran can be sorted out

indicators.note: a quarrel that can be sorted out, read as letters that can be put in a new order

explanation.surface: An optimistic diplomat thinks a quarrel with Iran is resolvable.
explanation.definitionFit: An aspirant is a candidate who aspires to something, a hopeful in the noun sense.

clue.text: Venetian magistrate naked on vacation, showing butt

parts.note: the doge was the elected chief magistrate of Venice

indicators.note: something on vacation is emptied out, so only the outside letters stay

parts.note: the word naked with its middle letters gone

explanation.surface: A Venetian official sunbathing nude on holiday, showing his backside.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Butt' suggests the bottom of a nudist, but it means a cigarette end.
explanation.definitionFit: A dog-end is British slang for a cigarette stub, which is also called a butt.

clue.text: Demand Far East buses can request this

parts.note: to exact payment is to demand it
taken as written
E is the compass abbreviation for east

explanation.surface: Bus companies in the Far East insist on something.
explanation.definitionFit: Some bus services take no change, so passengers must pay precisely the ticket price.

clue.text: Record love making event for dancers

parts.note: a disc is a gramophone record
love is zero in tennis, shaped like O

explanation.surface: A record about love-making, played at a dance.
explanation.definitionFit: A disco is a party or night out where people dance to recorded pop music.

clue.text: South American can start to need car

parts.note: S is the compass abbreviation for south
can is American slang for a toilet, which the British call the loo

indicators.note: start to means only the opening letter of the next word is used

explanation.surface: A South American who can't afford a car yet.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Can' looks like the verb, but it is the noun for a lavatory.
explanation.definitionFit: Saloon is the British word for a sedan, a car with a separate enclosed boot.

clue.text: Make error, literally picking up the perfect woman to marry

indicators.note: picking up a word is catching it by ear, so this signals a sound-alike

parts.note: Miss Right, the female version of Mr Right

explanation.surface: A man errs while chatting up his ideal bride.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Literally' here means in letters: the error is one of writing.
explanation.definitionFit: To miswrite is to write something incorrectly, a mistake made in the letters themselves.

clue.text: I am jumping into river in German city

indicators.note: jumping into a river puts the jumper inside it, so these letters go inside

parts.note: the Wear is a river in north-east England, through Durham
I am contracts to I'm

explanation.surface: Someone leaping into a river in a German city.
explanation.definitionFit: Weimar is a city in Thuringia, home of Goethe and namesake of the interwar republic.

clue.text: Forces United and Italian team to get people regularly dropped

parts.note: Inter Milan, the Italian football club

indicators.note: every other letter of the word people is dropped, leaving alternate ones

explanation.surface: Football talk: Manchester United and Inter, with players regularly dropped.
explanation.walkthrough: 'United' looks like a football club beside 'Italian team', but it belongs with 'Forces' in the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: Interpol is the International Criminal Police Organization, uniting the police forces of member nations.

clue.text: Care of tree rather dull and old fashioned

parts.note: a fir is a coniferous tree
staid means sedate, dull and old-fashioned

explanation.surface: A dreary, outdated method of looking after trees.
explanation.definitionFit: First aid is the immediate care given to an injured or ill person.

clue.text: Bar welcomes large group drooling

indicators.note: something that welcomes another takes it inside

parts.note: bar as a preposition means except, as does save
a ring is a group, such as a crime ring

explanation.surface: A pub receiving a big crowd of slobbering drinkers.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Bar' reads as a pub, but it is the preposition meaning except.
explanation.definitionFit: Slavering means letting saliva run from the mouth, the same as drooling.

clue.text: Lancashire lass returns with seeds, oddly, for badgers

indicators.note: returns means the name is read backwards

parts.note: Sarah Lancashire, the English actress of Coronation Street and Happy Valley

indicators.note: oddly means take the odd-numbered letters, first, third and fifth

explanation.surface: A northern girl comes back from the garden centre with seeds.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Lancashire lass' suggests any girl from that county, but it is the actress Sarah Lancashire.
explanation.definitionFit: To badger someone is to pester them persistently, which is what harassing means.

clue.text: Wear thin pants, as God intended

indicators.note: pants as British slang for rubbish signals that these letters are poorly arranged and need sorting

explanation.surface: Advice to wear flimsy underwear, as though divinely ordained.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Pants' looks like underwear; it is British slang meaning rubbish, here flagging an anagram.
explanation.definitionFit: Naked, the way one was born and so as nature or the Creator made one.

clue.text: Single politician is hot and playful

parts.note: I is the Roman numeral for one
MP is a Member of Parliament
H is the abbreviation for hot, as on taps

explanation.surface: An unmarried MP described as attractive and fun.
explanation.definitionFit: Impish means mischievous like an imp, so cheekily playful.

clue.text: Idiots going back over the hill

indicators.note: going back means the letters run in reverse

parts.note: a tit and a sap are both fools, so two idiots

explanation.surface: Fools retreating over a hill.
explanation.definitionFit: Past it means too old to do something well, as is being over the hill.

clue.text: How to tell if top is too tight to get flirty with someone

definitions.text: How to tell if top is too tight
definitions.meaning: first meaning: put the garment on to test the fit
second meaning: make a cheeky sexual advance or chance one's luck

explanation.walkthrough: The clothes-shop scene leads naturally into the cheeky advance; the phrase means both.
explanation.definitionFit: Trying a shirt on checks its fit, and trying it on with someone means making a pass at them.

clue.text: Kinky porn sale, in private

indicators.note: kinky means twisted, so the letters are bent into a new order

explanation.surface: A sale of racy material conducted behind closed doors.
explanation.definitionFit: Personal matters concern one individual and are kept away from others, hence private.

clue.text: Put forward assassin?

definitions.meaning: first meaning: present or propose something
second meaning: one who offs people, slang for killing them; the question mark flags an invented word

explanation.walkthrough: To off someone is slang for killing them, so a killer is one who offs; the question mark admits the coinage.
explanation.definitionFit: To present a proposal is to proffer it, and a hitman is literally one who offs people.

clue.text: On a cold and ultimately windy estate

parts.note: in cricket the on side is also called the leg side
C is the abbreviation for cold, as on taps

indicators.note: ultimately means only the final letter of the next word is used

explanation.surface: A country estate exposed to cold and, in the end, windy weather.
explanation.walkthrough: In cricket the leg side is the half of the field behind the batter's legs, also called the on side.
explanation.definitionFit: A legacy is property bequeathed in a will, and a dead person's property is their estate.

clue.text: Excited by nothing as much as you like

parts.note: agog means eagerly excited
O looks like zero, nothing

explanation.surface: Getting thrilled by nothing at all, as much as one wants.
explanation.definitionFit: Placed after a noun, the phrase means in abundance, without limit.

clue.text: Dictator's important little national symbol

indicators.note: a dictator speaks words for writing down, so what follows is as spoken

parts.note: key means important and wee, Scottish, means little

explanation.surface: A tyrant's prized small national emblem.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Dictator' suggests a despot, but it is one who dictates aloud.
explanation.definitionFit: The flightless kiwi bird is New Zealand's national emblem.

clue.text: Son caught with rotten food

parts.note: C is the cricket abbreviation for caught
food that has gone off is rotten

explanation.surface: A boy getting ill from bad food.
explanation.definitionFit: Scoff is informal British slang for grub or eats, as well as the verb to devour it.

clue.text: Tell me explosive is put around Communist leader

indicators.note: around means the shuffled letters wrap round the other piece
explosive letters are blown apart and land in a new order

parts.note: Tito, the communist ruler of Yugoslavia

explanation.surface: A demand for information about bombs planted around a communist leader.
explanation.definitionFit: Spit it out is an impatient urging to say something, the same as asking someone to tell me.

clue.text: Scolding German for beginning to destroy robe

indicators.note: for means one letter stands in place of another

parts.note: a dressing-down is a severe scolding

indicators.note: beginning to means only the opening letter of the next word

explanation.surface: A German being told off for starting to wreck a robe.
explanation.walkthrough: 'For' signals substitution: the G for German replaces the D from 'destroy' in the last word of the scolding phrase.
explanation.definitionFit: A dressing gown is a loose robe worn over nightclothes.
